topic: KV Cache Fragmentation Collapses Real-Time LLM Serving
postText:
Your GPU compute utilization sits at 35%, yet your production inference engine throws Out-Of-Memory errors and drops 40% of concurrent clinical requests.
I saw this firsthand running diagnostic summarization models in healthcare IT: raw compute is rarely the bottleneck—KV cache fragmentation is.

During auto-regressive generation, Large Language Models store Key and Value vectors for prior tokens in GPU VRAM. If your serving runtime allocates these segments as monolithic contiguous blocks based on worst-case sequence limits, internal memory fragmentation rapidly exhausts physical VRAM. Erratic patient intake notes quickly shatter memory space, crashing high-concurrency instances.

We stabilized our inference pipeline with three architectural patterns:
1. Paged KV Allocation: Divide context storage into fixed-size virtual blocks allocated non-contiguously across VRAM.
2. Speculative Memory Offloading: Evict idle conversation sequences to host system RAM during asynchronous model tool calls.
3. Dynamic Request Quotas: Enforce strict token ceiling limits to prevent pathological context bloat.

Hardware scale cannot cure naive memory layouts.

How does your inference stack handle KV cache exhaustion during burst traffic—engine-level paging, request preemption, or rigid concurrency caps?
